anomalies.observed: The anodes of the three status LEDs D8 (green), D15 (green) and D27 (yellow) sit only on net /NET0060. No other pin is on that net, so the anodes have no supply connection. Their cathodes go through R77, R50 and R1 to the CM4 Ethernet and activity nLED outputs (Module2 pins 15, 17 and 21).
anomalies.expected: Common-anode status LEDs driven through a current-limiting resistor from the cathode side need their anodes on the +3V3 rail. The other status LEDs in this netlist (D26, D41, D9) take their anodes from +3V3 through R45, R47 or directly.
anomalies.impact: The three status LEDs cannot light, so the Ethernet link/activity and the related indicator functions give no visible feedback. This is probably a missing connection from the anode net to +3V3 (a removed or unrouted wire).

anomalies.observed: R5 is labelled with value "24k" but its library description and MPN are for a 24Ω 0805 resistor (FRC0805J240TSD, "24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor"). R5 is placed across the high-voltage PoE-style output rail VOUTP–VOUTN.
anomalies.expected: The resistor's value field should match the part being ordered. Across a rail of tens of volts, a 24Ω part would dissipate about 135 W at 57 V, so a 24Ω part here would be destroyed; a 24kΩ value would have been intended instead.

evidence.quote: (comp (ref "R5") (value "24k") (footprint "Resistor_SMD:R_0805_2012Metric") ... (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS")

anomalies.impact: If the board is built from this BOM, the wrong part (24Ω instead of 24kΩ) would be fitted across the high-voltage output. This would draw large current, overheat the 0805 resistor and load the rail heavily.

parsed.summary: Two candidate deviations were found: the anodes of status LEDs D8, D15 and D27 are on a net with no supply connection, so they cannot light, and R5 is specified as 24k but its library part is a 24Ω resistor across the high-voltage output rail. The rest of the netlist (power paths, CAN, USB, Ethernet, PoE, I2C and SPI routing) appears consistent with the schematic intent.
